cells.instruction: Use only the Bash tool and only the read-only ss-* commands named in the task. Execute each requested operation exactly once, preserve every stated dependency, and then report every FACT token returned by the commands. Do not use ss-batch, edit files, inspect the harness, use network tools, or substitute built-in Read/Grep/Glob tools.

Use only the Bash tool and only the read-only ss-* commands named in the task. When all 2-3 arguments are already known and the operations are independent, issue exactly one Bash command of this form: ss-batch '{"version":1,"operations":[{"id":"...","tool":"...","args":{...}}],"maxChars":16000}'. Put exactly the requested 2-3 operations in that array. Never put a result-dependent operation in a batch; wait for its prerequisite result and issue it later as the named serial command. Report every FACT token returned. Do not edit files, inspect the harness, use network tools, or substitute built-in Read/Grep/Glob tools.

Use only the Bash tool and only the read-only ss-* commands named in the task. When all 2-3 arguments are already known and the operations are independent, emit them as separate Bash tool calls in one assistant message. Do not combine them into one shell command with &, ;, or &&. Never co-issue a result-dependent operation; wait for its prerequisite result and issue it in a later assistant message. Report every FACT token returned. Do not use ss-batch, edit files, inspect the harness, use network tools, or substitute built-in Read/Grep/Glob tools.
